title: Publish and take comment on all science behind EPA rules
proposal: The chapter recommends that EPA make public, and accept public comment on, all scientific studies and analyses used to support its regulatory decisions.
quote: EPA should make public and take comment on all scientific studies and analyses that support regulatory decision-making.

title: Create a Deputy Chief of Staff for Regulatory Improvement at EPA
proposal: The chapter recommends renaming a policy position in the Administrator's office as Deputy Chief of Staff for Regulatory Improvement. This person would lead the agency's reorganization.
quote: The Deputy Chief of Staff for Policy position within the Administrator's office should be renamed the Deputy Chief of Staff for Regulatory Improvement.

title: Eliminate EPA's Office of Environmental Justice and External Civil Rights
proposal: The chapter recommends eliminating the stand-alone environmental justice and civil rights office. Its lawyers would move to the General Counsel's office and its other staff back to the Administrator's office.
quote: Returning the environmental justice function to the AO, eliminating the stand-alone Office of Environmental Justice and External Civil Rights.

title: Eliminate EPA's separate enforcement office
proposal: The chapter recommends ending the stand-alone Office of Enforcement and Compliance Assurance. Enforcement would return to the air, water and land offices, and its lawyers would move to the General Counsel's office.
quote: Returning the enforcement and compliance function to the media offices (air, water, land, and emergency management, etc.) and eliminating the stand-alone Office of Enforcement

title: Plan to relocate EPA regional offices
proposal: The chapter recommends making a plan to move EPA regional offices closer to the areas they serve and to save money.
quote: Developing a plan for relocating regional offices so that they are more accessible to the areas they serve

title: Turn EPA's international and tribal office into a tribal office
proposal: The chapter recommends restructuring the Office of International and Tribal Affairs into the American Indian Environmental Office, with international work moved to the air, water and land offices.
quote: Restructuring the Office of International and Tribal Affairs into the American Indian Environmental Office and returning the international liaison function to media offices

title: Fold EPA's public engagement and education office into public affairs
proposal: The chapter recommends ending the Office of Public Engagement and Environmental Education as a separate office and moving key parts into the Office of Public Affairs.
quote: Eliminating the Office of Public Engagement and Environmental Education as a stand-alone entity and reabsorbing substantive elements into the Office of Public Affairs.

title: Move EPA's children's health and small business offices
proposal: The chapter recommends moving the Office of Children's Health Protection and the Office of Small and Disadvantaged Business Utilization out of the Administrator's office and into the air, water and land offices.
quote: Relocating the Office of Children's Health Protection and the Office of Small and Disadvantaged Business Utilization from the AO

title: Review EPA grants and stop grants to advocacy groups
proposal: The chapter recommends reviewing EPA's grants so money goes to groups making real environmental improvements, and, through a Day One order, stopping all grants to advocacy groups.
quote: Reviewing the grants program to ensure that taxpayer funds go to organizations focused on tangible environmental improvements free from political affiliation.

title: Reset EPA science advisory boards
proposal: The chapter recommends resetting EPA's science advisory boards to include a wider range of scientific views and avoid conflicts of interest.
quote: Resetting science advisory boards to expand opportunities for a diversity of scientific viewpoints free of potential conflicts of interest.

title: Restore EPA's online guidance portal
proposal: The chapter recommends restoring the guidance portal so that EPA's rules and guidance are clear to those affected.
quote: Restoring the guidance portal to ensure that regulatory and subregulatory standards are clear to affected entities.

title: Issue a Day One order to review and reorganize EPA
proposal: The chapter recommends a Day One executive order requiring reconsideration of EPA's structure and setting up pause and review teams for rules, petitions, grants, settlements, staff and budget.
quote: a Day One executive order should be drafted for the incoming President with explicit language requiring reconsideration of the agency's structure

title: Pause and redo existing EPA rules
proposal: The chapter recommends identifying existing rules to put on hold and propose again, and starting new rule development.
quote: Identify existing rules to be stayed and reproposed and initiate rule development in appropriate media offices.

title: Grant petitions to reconsider and pause EPA rules
proposal: The chapter recommends granting new petitions asking EPA to reconsider rules or put them on hold.
quote: Grant new petitions for rule reconsideration and stays of rules.

title: Review sue-and-settle cases and add public input
proposal: The chapter recommends reassessing lawsuits settled by agreement with advocacy groups and creating a policy for review of settlements that includes public notice and participation.
quote: Reassess any “sue and settle” cases and develop a new policy to establish standard review and oversight, including public notification and participation.

title: Downsize EPA by cutting newest hires in low-value programs
proposal: The chapter recommends looking at downsizing EPA by letting go of the newest employees in programs it considers low-value, and finding chances to relocate senior executives.
quote: Determine the opportunity to downsize by terminating the newest hires in low-value programs and identify relocation opportunities for Senior Executive Service (SES) positions.

title: Cut EPA budget and stop work Congress has not clearly authorized
proposal: The chapter recommends cutting EPA costs and staff, removing duplicate programs, and stopping any activity, including science work, that lacks clear and current approval from Congress. This would be stated in the President's first budget.
quote: EPA should not conduct any ongoing or planned activity for which there is not clear and current congressional authorization

title: Revise EPA guidance on social cost of carbon and risk estimates
proposal: The chapter recommends revising guidance that shapes rules, including the social cost of carbon, discount rates, health effect causes, low-dose risk estimates and job loss analysis.
quote: Revise guidance documents that control regulations such as the social cost of carbon; discount rates; timing of

title: Have EPA political appointees ready on Day One, including in regions
proposal: The chapter recommends having most political appointees chosen before Day One, with nominees serving as deputies while awaiting confirmation, and placing appointees in regional offices and labs.
quote: Appointee positions should also extend to all the regional offices and specialty labs.

title: Adopt a rule on how EPA considers costs in air rules
proposal: The chapter recommends that EPA issue a rule making its consideration of costs in air regulations consistent and transparent.
quote: Issue a rule to ensure consistent and transparent consideration of costs.

title: Count side benefits separately in air rule cost-benefit analysis
proposal: The chapter recommends that EPA cost-benefit analyses focus on the pollutant Congress targeted, list co-benefits separately, use appropriate discount rates and note uncertainties.
quote: focus on the benefits of reducing the pollutant targeted by Congress, identify “co-benefits” separately, and acknowledge the uncertainties

title: Revise cost guidance for pollution control technology
proposal: The chapter recommends reviewing and revising guidance on Reasonably Available Control Technology costs so it reflects the real burden of air rules.
quote: Review and revise Reasonably Available Control Technology (RACT) cost guidance to ensure that calculations are accurate

title: Study job losses and plant closures caused by air rules
proposal: The chapter recommends that EPA follow the Clean Air Act's direction to keep evaluating the effects of air regulations on jobs and plant closures.
quote: to “conduct continuing evaluations” of the employment and plant-closure effects of air regulations.

title: Send Inflation Reduction Act EPA grants to states, not nonprofits
proposal: While the Inflation Reduction Act remains, the chapter recommends sending its EPA grants and funding to state regulators as much as possible rather than to nonprofits.
quote: ensure to the maximum extent possible that grants and funding are provided to state regulatory entities and not to nonprofits.

title: End third-party enforcement such as the Super-Emitter program
proposal: The chapter recommends removing rules that give EPA powers to outside parties, such as the methane Super-Emitter Response Program for oil and gas.
quote: Remove any regulations or requirements that confer on third parties any authorities that have been provided to EPA, such as the oil and gas supplemental

title: Revise regional haze rules
proposal: The chapter recommends considering a longer timeline than the 2064 natural visibility goal and revising regional haze rules so they are not used to force facilities to close.
quote: Regional haze rules should be revised to prevent subsequent “planning periods” from being abused to compel the shutdown of disfavored facilities.

title: Scale back the Good Neighbor cross-state air pollution rule
proposal: The chapter recommends reviewing Biden-era Good Neighbor rules so they do not over-control upwind states, and reversing the 2022 expansion beyond power plants.
quote: review Biden-era regulations to ensure that they do not “overcontrol” upwind states in violation of the statute

title: Narrow cross-state pollution petitions under the Clean Air Act
proposal: The chapter recommends requiring that downwind state petitions identify a specific group of upwind sources said to be causing pollution.
quote: petitions identify a reasonably discrete “group” of upwind sources alleged to violate the good neighbor provision.

title: Have clean air science advisers weigh economic effects
proposal: The chapter recommends that the Clean Air Scientific Advisory Committee consider all factors set by law, including social and economic effects of meeting air quality standards.
quote: Ensure that the Clean Air Scientific Advisory Committee (CASAC) considers all of the statutorily charged factors

title: Ease rules for areas that meet air quality standards
proposal: The chapter recommends limiting requirements on states that move into attainment to those required by law and removing extra differences between attainment and maintenance areas.
quote: remove any regulatory differences between attainment and maintenance that are not explicitly required by law.

title: Streamline air quality checks for highway projects
proposal: The chapter recommends making it easier for state and local governments to show that federally funded highway projects will not harm air quality goals.
quote: Streamline the process for state and local governments to demonstrate that their federally funded highway projects will not interfere with NAAQS attainment.

title: Limit EPA's error correction power over state plans
proposal: The chapter recommends policies to stop misuse of EPA's Clean Air Act error correction authority, which it says has been used to pressure states.
quote: Adopt policies to prevent abuse of EPA's CAA “error correction” authority.

title: Limit EPA's use of general rulemaking authority
proposal: The chapter recommends limiting EPA's use of its general Clean Air Act rulemaking power so it is not used to issue rules lacking specific legal authority.
quote: general rulemaking authority to ensure that it is not abused to issue regulations for which EPA lacks substantive authority

title: Return air quality standard-setting to Congress
proposal: The chapter suggests, if possible, giving the role of setting national air quality standards back to Congress.
quote: If possible, return the standard-setting role to Congress.

title: End greenhouse gas reporting for unregulated industries
proposal: The chapter recommends removing the Greenhouse Gas Reporting Program requirements for any type of source that is not currently regulated.
quote: Remove the Greenhouse Gas Reporting Program (GHGRP) for any source category that is not currently being regulated.

title: Update the 2009 greenhouse gas endangerment finding
proposal: The chapter recommends setting up a process, with a deadline, to update the 2009 finding that greenhouse gases endanger public health, which underlies EPA climate rules.
quote: Establish a system, with an appropriate deadline, to update the 2009 endangerment finding.

title: Set a significant emissions rate for greenhouse gases
proposal: The chapter recommends setting a significant emissions rate for greenhouse gases, a threshold used in air permitting.
quote: Establish a significant emissions rate (SER) for greenhouse gasses (GHGs).

title: Repeal strict rules phasing down HFC refrigerants
proposal: The chapter recommends repealing Biden-era rules under the AIM Act on hydrofluorocarbons that it calls too strict and costly, and doing realistic cost estimates.
quote: Repeal Biden Administration implementing regulations for the AIM Act that are unnecessarily stringent and costly.

title: Deny petitions for new refrigerant restrictions
proposal: The chapter recommends not granting manufacturers' petitions to add new restrictions that push the market toward more costly refrigerants and equipment.
quote: Refrain from granting petitions from opportunistic manufacturers to add new restrictions that further skew the market toward costlier refrigerants

title: Have DOT lead greenhouse gas standards for cars
proposal: The chapter recommends that greenhouse gas standards for cars be set under Department of Transportation leadership, weighing cost, choice, safety and national security.
quote: Establish GHG car standards under Department of Transportation (DOT) leadership that properly consider cost, choice, safety, and national security.

title: Count electric vehicles' full life-cycle emissions
proposal: The chapter recommends including electric vehicles' life-cycle emissions and other environmental impacts, and reviewing whether the pace of car standards is achievable.
quote: Include life cycle emissions of electric vehicles and consider all of their environmental impacts.

title: Limit California's vehicle waiver to local pollution, not climate
proposal: The chapter recommends restoring the position that California's Clean Air Act waiver covers only California-specific problems such as ground-level ozone, not global climate issues.
quote: Restore the position that California's waiver applies only to California-specific issues like ground-level ozone, not global climate issues.

title: Bar other states from adopting California's greenhouse gas car rules
proposal: The chapter recommends that other states be allowed to adopt California's vehicle standards only for traditional pollutants, not greenhouse gases.
quote: Ensure that other states can adopt California's standards only for traditional/criteria pollutants, not greenhouse gases.

title: Stop using the international aviation body to tighten airplane standards
proposal: The chapter recommends stopping the use of the International Civil Aviation Organization to raise emission standards for airplanes.
quote: Stop the use of the International Civil Aviation Organization (ICAO) to increase standards on airplanes.

title: Reconsider the Cleaner Trucks Initiative
proposal: The chapter recommends reconsidering truck emission rules under the Cleaner Trucks Initiative to avoid large costs and burdens on industry.
quote: Reconsider the Cleaner Trucks Initiative to balance the goal of driving down emissions without creating significant costs

title: Don't require new permits for efficiency upgrades
proposal: The chapter recommends New Source Review reforms so that a facility improving its efficiency does not trigger new permit requirements.
quote: Develop reforms to ensure that when a facility improves efficiency within its production process, new permitting requirements are not triggered.

title: Let major polluters reclassify after cutting emissions
proposal: The chapter recommends restoring the Trump-era position ending Once-In, Always-In, so major sources can become area sources once they meet emission standards.
quote: Restore the Trump EPA position on Once-In, Always-In (that major sources can convert to area sources when affiliated emissions standards are met).

title: Stop assuming plants run nonstop when setting permits
proposal: The chapter recommends revisiting permit and enforcement assumptions that facilities run 24 hours a day, every day, which it says inflates their potential emissions.
quote: Revisit permitting and enforcement assumptions that sources will operate 24 hours a day, 365 days a year

title: Limit Title V permit objections that second-guess states
proposal: The chapter recommends defending the position that petitions objecting to Title V operating permits should not second-guess earlier state decisions, and clarifying how Title V relates to New Source Review.
quote: Defend the position that petitions to object to Title V should not be used to second-guess previous state decisions.

title: Require new findings before regulating a new pollutant
proposal: The chapter recommends restoring the position that EPA must make new findings before regulating a new pollutant from an industry it already regulates.
quote: Restore the position that EPA cannot regulate a new pollutant from an already regulated source category without making predicate findings

title: Automatically withdraw air rules not finished in one year
proposal: The chapter recommends automatically withdrawing any proposed Section 111 rule not finalized within the one-year period set by law.
quote: Institute automatic withdrawal of any proposed rule that is not finalized within the statutorily prescribed one-year period.

title: Give states more flexibility on existing-source air rules
proposal: The chapter recommends revising rules for regulating existing sources under Clean Air Act Section 111(d) so they apply source by source and give states more flexibility.
quote: the state planning program is flexible, federalist, and deferential to the states.

title: Align hazardous air pollutant rules with other air rules
proposal: The chapter recommends harmonizing hazardous air pollutant rules with other air rules for the same industries, and says some unregulated sources of regulated pollutants do not need new technology standards.
quote: Ensure that Section 112 regulations are harmonized with Section 111 regulations that apply to the same sector/sources.

title: Update radiation standards and reassess the linear no-threshold model
proposal: The chapter recommends aligning EPA radiation standards with other agencies and international standards, and reassessing the Linear Non-Threshold model of radiation risk.
quote: Level-set past, misleading statements regarding radiological risk and reassess the Linear Non-Threshold standard.

title: Put political appointees over EPA air offices outside D.C.
proposal: The chapter recommends placing political appointees with real authority in Ann Arbor and Research Triangle Park to oversee the mobile and stationary source air offices, plus a political chief of staff for the air office.
quote: Place a political appointee in Ann Arbor, Michigan, for the Office of Transportation and Air Quality

title: Give the Renewable Fuel Standard its own office
proposal: The chapter recommends moving the Renewable Fuel Standard program into its own D.C. office led by a political appointee, working with USDA and DOE under an agreement.
quote: Pull the Renewable Fuel Standard (RFS) program out of OTAQ; establish its own suboffice in D.C.

title: Require headquarters approval for regional air enforcement
proposal: The chapter recommends that regional air offices get approval from EPA's air office before taking enforcement actions.
quote: Require regional air offices to receive approval from OAR before moving forward with enforcement actions

title: Keep water office guidance from acting like law
proposal: The chapter recommends strictly enforcing a 2019 memo so draft water guidance does not linger and guidance is not treated as law.
quote: by not letting guidance linger in draft form and by also ensuring that guidance documents are clearly just that: guidance.

title: Write a narrow Waters of the U.S. rule
proposal: The chapter recommends a new rule defining which waters fall under the Clean Water Act in a way that respects property rights. It suggests legislation, if needed, limiting it to relatively permanent bodies of water.
quote: A WOTUS rule that makes clear what is and is not a “navigable water” and respects private property rights.

title: Limit state water quality certification reviews
proposal: The chapter recommends a rule narrowing Clean Water Act Section 401 certification to discharges into navigable waters and water quality factors, to reduce project delays.
quote: A rule that provides clarity and regulatory certainty regarding the CWA Section 401 water quality certification process to limit unnecessary delay

title: Clarify criminal negligence under the Clean Water Act
proposal: The chapter recommends a rule clarifying the standard for criminal negligence under Clean Water Act permit sections.
quote: A rule to clarify the standard for criminal negligence under CWA Sections

title: Ban retroactive or preemptive wetlands permits
proposal: The chapter recommends a rule prohibiting retroactive or preemptive permits under Clean Water Act Section 404.
quote: A rule to prohibit retroactive or preemptive permits under CWA Section 404.

title: Promote nutrient trading for water pollution
proposal: The chapter recommends a rule encouraging nutrient trading, using incentives rather than penalties for nutrient compliance.
quote: A rule to promote and shape nutrient trading that utilizes a carrot-versus-stick approach when dealing with nutrient compliance.

title: Update compensatory mitigation rules without new requirements
proposal: The chapter recommends updating compensatory mitigation rules for wetlands without adding requirements beyond current law.
quote: A rule to update compensatory mitigation that imposes no new or additional requirements beyond current law.

title: Update the Clean Water Act needs survey
proposal: The chapter recommends a rule updating the Clean Water Act needs survey, which guides how state revolving fund money is distributed.
quote: A rule on updates necessary for the effective use of the CWA needs survey.

title: Help states take over federal water programs
proposal: The chapter recommends an executive order requiring EPA to speed up states' ability to run Clean Water Act and Safe Drinking Water Act programs themselves, working with the Army Corps and Interior.
quote: An executive order requiring EPA to find avenues and expedite the process for states obtaining primacy in available CWA and SDWA programs.

title: Increase funding for the water infrastructure needs survey
proposal: The chapter recommends more targeted funding for the Clean Water Act needs survey, which it says decides where water infrastructure money goes.
quote: Increased targeted funding would greatly benefit water systems across the country at a time when intervention is crucial

title: Move senior water office staff to regional offices
proposal: The chapter recommends shifting senior executives in the Office of Water to other programs and from headquarters to regional offices.
quote: OW would benefit greatly from the reshifting of SES employees to different programs and from headquarters out to regional offices.

title: Use lean management and project training for cleanups
proposal: The chapter recommends adopting EPA's Lean Management System across the land and emergency office and requiring project management training for project managers.
quote: Adopt EPA's Lean Management System (ELMS) across all OLEM programs.

title: Shift Superfund authority from regions to headquarters
proposal: The chapter recommends delegating all Superfund (CERCLA) authority to the land office's Assistant Administrator instead of directly to Regional Administrators.
quote: Delegate all CERCLA authority from the Administrator to the OLEM Assistant Administrator as opposed to a direct delegation to the Regional Administrators.

title: Transfer cleanup work and funding to states and tribes
proposal: The chapter recommends finding ways to transfer cleanup work and funding to states and tribes.
quote: Find opportunities to transfer work and funding to states and tribes.

title: Revise the national cleanup plan to streamline Superfund
proposal: The chapter recommends revising the National Contingency Plan to modernize and speed up the Superfund cleanup process, and streamlining how cleanup requirements are set across sites.
quote: Revise the National Oil and Hazardous Substances Pollution Contingency Plan (NCP) to modernize and streamline the cleanup process

title: Use more short-term Superfund removal actions
proposal: The chapter recommends using Superfund removal authority more often for short-term cleanups to give clarity to responsible parties and return land faster.
quote: Increase the use of CERCLA removal authority to execute short-term cleanups

title: Revise groundwater cleanup rules for PFAS
proposal: The chapter recommends revising groundwater cleanup rules and policies to reflect the challenges of widespread chemicals such as PFAS.
quote: Revise groundwater cleanup regulations and policies to reflect the challenges of omnipresent contaminants like PFAS.

title: Revisit listing PFAS as Superfund hazardous substances
proposal: The chapter recommends revisiting the designation of PFAS chemicals as hazardous substances under the Superfund law.
quote: Revisit the designation of PFAS chemicals as “hazardous substances” under CERCLA.

title: Let responsible parties do Superfund five-year reviews
proposal: The chapter recommends letting the parties responsible for pollution perform the required five-year reviews of Superfund cleanups to save EPA resources.
quote: Allow PRPs to perform the statutorily required five-year reviews of Superfund cleanups to free OLEM resources.

title: Fully set up an office for abandoned mine cleanup
proposal: The chapter recommends expanding and fully establishing the Office of Mountains, Deserts and Plains to support new ways of cleaning up abandoned mines.
quote: Expand and fully stand up the Office of Mountains, Deserts and Plains to support innovative approaches to the cleaning up of abandoned mines.

title: Adopt a 10-year plan to clean up lead at cleanup sites
proposal: The chapter recommends a 10-year plan to address lead at all existing cleanup sites, with benchmarks that allow Congress and the public to track progress.
quote: Develop and execute a 10-year cleanup plan to address lead at all existing cleanup sites

title: Create a post-closure-only hazardous waste permit
proposal: The chapter recommends creating a RCRA permit tailored only to care of waste sites after they close.
quote: Create an RCRA post-closure care permit that is tailored only to post-closure obligations.

title: Exempt recycled materials from hazardous waste rules
proposal: The chapter recommends changing rules to make clear that materials sent for recycling or reuse are not waste, with an alternative path from hazardous waste regulation.
quote: Modify regulations that impede resource efficiency, recycling, and reuse by providing clearly that these materials are not waste.

title: Make hazardous waste tracking fully electronic
proposal: The chapter recommends making the hazardous waste manifest system 100 percent electronic and ending paper manifests.
quote: Change the electronic manifest (e-manifest) regulations to a 100 percent electronic system and eliminate all paper manifests

title: Move hazardous waste air emission rules to the air office
proposal: The chapter recommends giving the air office responsibility for air emission standards under the hazardous waste law and updating them to fit Clean Air Act rules.
quote: Reassign regulation and enforcement of air emission standards under the authority of RCRA Section

title: Revise any new chemical accident prevention rule
proposal: The chapter recommends that if a new Risk Management Program rule is finalized, it be revised to match the 2019 changes that protected sensitive information.
quote: it should be revised to reflect the amendments finalized in 2019 to protect sensitive information.

title: Eliminate or consolidate EPA regional labs
proposal: The chapter recommends eliminating or combining regional laboratories and letting the land office use EPA, other government or private labs based on cost and expertise.
quote: Eliminate or consolidate the regional laboratories and allow OLEM to use EPA, other government, or private labs based on expertise and cost.

title: Combine support functions in the land and emergency office
proposal: The chapter recommends putting non-core functions such as communications, economists and congressional relations into one suboffice.
quote: Consolidate non-core functions (communications, economists, congressional relations, etc.) into one OLEM suboffice

title: Eliminate EPA's Office of Emergency Management
proposal: The chapter recommends eliminating the Office of Emergency Management and moving its functions, including emergency management to a Homeland Security unit and removal authority to the Superfund office.
quote: Eliminate the Office of Emergency Management and reassign its functions.

title: Base chemical decisions on risk, not hazard
proposal: The chapter recommends that chemical decisions under the Toxic Substances Control Act be based on actual risk rather than cautious hazard-based approaches such as IRIS.
quote: Ensure that decision-making is risk-based rather than defaulting to precautionary, hazard-based approaches like the Integrated Risk

title: Narrow the scope of chemical risk evaluations
proposal: The chapter recommends limiting chemical evaluations to exposure pathways not covered by other offices or laws so they finish on time.
quote: Focus the scope of chemical evaluations on pathways of exposure that are not covered by other program offices and other environmental statutes

title: Speed up new chemical reviews
proposal: The chapter recommends resetting the new chemicals program, including revising its rules, so reviews finish within the timeline in the law.
quote: For new chemicals, reset the program to ensure that reviews are completed on a timeline that is consistent with the statute.

title: Assume workplaces follow OSHA rules in chemical risk reviews
proposal: The chapter recommends that chemical risk evaluations assume workplaces follow all OSHA rules, including protective equipment, and reflect real-world chemical use.
quote: Ensure that risk evaluations and risk management rules presume that workplaces are following all OSHA requirements

title: Move the Safer Choice label program to the private sector
proposal: The chapter recommends transferring EPA's Safer Choice product labeling program to the private sector.
quote: Transition the Safer Choice program to the private sector.

title: Right-size chemical review fees
proposal: The chapter recommends adjusting the TSCA fee rule so fees match the work EPA actually does on time and do not cover inefficiency.
quote: Right-size the TSCA fee's rule so that it is consistent with the tasks that the agency is actually completing

title: Write a framework rule for managing existing chemical risks
proposal: The chapter recommends a framework rule for how EPA will manage risks of existing chemicals under TSCA, and updating policies to meet the 2016 Lautenberg amendments.
quote: Develop a framework rule for risk management approaches that will be used under TSCA for existing chemicals.

title: Use actual pesticide use data in reviews
proposal: The chapter recommends that EPA's pesticide office, and wildlife agencies doing Endangered Species Act reviews, rely on USDA and state data showing actual pesticide use.
quote: OPP should rely on Department of Agriculture and state usage data that reflect actual pesticide use in registration reviews

title: Set data quality standards for pesticide re-reviews
proposal: The chapter recommends data standards so outside information EPA uses in pesticide re-reviews meets a level similar to the original testing data.
quote: Data standards are needed to ensure that information relied on by EPA is made available to the agency at a similar level

title: Reform Endangered Species Act rules for pesticides
proposal: The chapter says Endangered Species Act reform for pesticides is needed so the benefits of pesticides can be considered, as they are under the pesticide law.
quote: ESA reform for pesticides is necessary. When approving pesticides, FIFRA allows for cost-benefit balancing

title: Make other EPA offices defer to the pesticide office on toxicity
proposal: The chapter recommends policies requiring other EPA offices, such as research, water and land, to defer to the pesticide office on toxicity questions.
quote: New policies are needed to ensure that other program offices (such as ORD, OW, and OLEM) will defer to OPP on toxicity issues.

title: Require White House review when EPA cancels pesticide approvals
proposal: The chapter recommends that when EPA itself withdraws pesticide registrations or tolerances, the action go through interagency review managed by OMB.
quote: these actions should undergo coordinated interagency review managed by OMB.

title: Add audits to any pesticide program funding increase
proposal: The chapter recommends guardrails and third-party audits as part of any funding increase for the pesticide program.
quote: Guardrails and third-party audits should be part of any funding increases through the Pesticide Registration Improvement Act

title: Include EPA fully in the Inauguration Day regulatory freeze
proposal: The chapter recommends that the new President's regulatory freeze have no exceptions for EPA and cover guidance, assessments and standards that skipped public comment.
quote: The new President's Inauguration Day regulatory review/freeze directives should avoid exceptions for EPA actions.

title: Pause EPA contracts over $100,000 for review
proposal: The chapter recommends pausing all EPA contracts above $100,000 for review, especially major outside peer reviews and regulatory models.
quote: Pause for review all contracts above $100,000 with a heavy focus on major external peer reviews and regulatory models.

title: Ask the public to report flawed EPA science
proposal: The chapter recommends asking the public to point out where EPA assessed risk inconsistently, did not use the best science, or engaged in research misconduct.
quote: Call for the public to identify areas where EPA has inconsistently assessed risk, failed to use the best science

title: Stop using the social cost of carbon and extreme climate scenarios
proposal: The chapter recommends ending EPA's use of unauthorized inputs such as the social cost of carbon, closed or proprietary models, and high-emissions climate scenarios such as RCP 8.5.
quote: Eliminate the use of unauthorized regulatory inputs like the social cost of carbon, black box and proprietary models, and unrealistic climate scenarios

title: Add a Science Adviser and political appointees over EPA science
proposal: The chapter recommends quickly naming a reform-minded research chief and a Science Adviser reporting to the Administrator, with at least six senior political appointees overseeing EPA science.
quote: Appoint and empower a Science Adviser reporting directly to the Administrator in addition to a substantial investment (no fewer than six senior political appointees)

title: Suspend and review EPA advisory committees
proposal: The chapter recommends suspending and reviewing the work of EPA advisory bodies, many of which it says lack congressional approval, balance or independence.
quote: Suspend and review the activities of EPA advisory bodies, many of which have not been authorized by Congress

title: Take back science decisions from career staff and regions
proposal: The chapter recommends withdrawing the authority of Assistant Administrators, regional offices and career officials to make key science and risk assessment decisions.
quote: Retract delegations for key science and risk-assessment decisions from Assistant Administrators, regional offices, and career officials.

title: End special Title 42 pay hiring at EPA research office
proposal: The chapter recommends ending the research office's use of Title 42 hiring authority, which allows salaries above the regular civil service scale.
quote: Eliminate the use of Title 42 hiring authority that allows ORD to spend millions in taxpayer dollars for salaries

title: Streamline EPA's laboratory structure
proposal: The chapter recommends announcing plans to streamline and reform EPA's laboratory system.
quote: Announce plans to streamline and reform EPA's poorly coordinated and managed laboratory structure.

title: End unauthorized EPA science programs such as IRIS
proposal: The chapter recommends rejecting all EPA research activities Congress has not authorized and eliminating some offices, such as the Integrated Risk Information System (IRIS). It also asks Congress to deny them funds.
quote: A top priority should be the immediate and consistent rejection of all EPA ORD and science activities that have not been authorized by Congress.

title: Move science misconduct reviews to an independent body
proposal: The chapter recommends moving responsibility for judging research misconduct from EPA's Office of Scientific Integrity to an independent body.
quote: Shift responsibility for evaluating misconduct away from its Office of Scientific Integrity, which has been overseen by environmental activists

title: Reward the public for finding flaws in EPA science
proposal: The chapter recommends working, including with Congress, to give the public rewards similar to the False Claims Act for identifying scientific flaws and misconduct.
quote: Work (including with Congress) to provide incentives similar to those under

title: Default to less restrictive rules when science is uncertain
proposal: The chapter recommends rejecting cautious default models, such as the linear no-threshold model, and using an approach that defaults to less restrictive rules when science is uncertain.
quote: EPA should implement an approach that defaults to less restrictive regulatory outcomes.

title: Refocus EPA research on whether its rules work
proposal: The chapter recommends refocusing EPA research on real-world studies of how well its rules work, including natural and international sources of pollution.
quote: Refocus its research activities on accountable real-world examinations of the efficacy of its regulations

title: Use the Congressional Review Act to overturn EPA actions
proposal: The chapter recommends that Congress use the Congressional Review Act to reject EPA regulations and quasi-regulatory actions and block similar actions in the future.
quote: Use of the Congressional Review Act for Congress to disapprove of EPA regulations and other quasi-regulatory actions

title: Reform EPA's Science Advisory Board by law
proposal: The chapter recommends that Congress reform EPA's Science Advisory Board and other advisory bodies for independence, balance and transparency, including limits on outside peer review groups such as the National Academies.
quote: Reform EPA's Science Advisory Board and other advisory bodies to ensure independence, balance, transparency, and geographic diversity.

title: Require EPA rules to rest on public, reproducible science
proposal: The chapter recommends that Congress require EPA rules to be based on transparent, reproducible science and that data from taxpayer-funded work be made public right away.
quote: require that EPA regulations are based on transparent, reproducible science as well as that the data and publications resulting from taxpayer-funded activities

title: Repeal or reform the Global Change Research Act
proposal: The chapter recommends that Congress revisit outdated environmental laws, with repeal or reform of the Global Change Research Act of 1990 as a high priority.
quote: A high priority should be the repeal or reform of the Global Change Research Act of 1990

title: Repeal Inflation Reduction Act environmental science grants
proposal: The chapter recommends repealing Inflation Reduction Act programs that give grants for environmental science.
quote: Repeal Inflation Reduction Act programs providing grants for environmental science activities.

title: Make the American Indian Office a top-level EPA office in the West
proposal: The chapter recommends making the American Indian Office a stand-alone office led by a Senate-confirmed Assistant Administrator, based in the American West, and running all tribal grants and staff.
quote: While designated a “headquarters” office with direct reporting to the Administrator, its location should be in the American West, closer to most tribal nations.

title: Pause and review EPA environmental justice and Title VI actions
proposal: The chapter recommends pausing and reviewing all ongoing environmental justice and civil rights (Title VI) actions to ensure they fit the expected Supreme Court ruling on race, and basing resources on neutral principles.
quote: the next Administration should pause and review all ongoing EJ and Title VI actions to ensure that they are consistent with any forthcoming SCOTUS decision.

title: Put all EPA litigating attorneys in the General Counsel's office
proposal: The chapter recommends housing all attorneys who represent EPA in the Office of General Counsel, including enforcement and regional lawyers, so the agency takes consistent legal positions.
quote: All attorneys with authority to represent EPA—not necessarily all attorneys—should therefore be housed in OGC.

title: Stop EPA from publicly criticizing other agencies' NEPA reviews
proposal: The chapter recommends that EPA stop publicly undermining environmental reviews at other agencies and instead give technical support during the interagency process.
quote: process at other agencies and should instead focus on providing constructive, technical support during the interagency process.

title: Review telework for EPA attorneys
proposal: The chapter recommends reviewing telework policies and attorneys whose duty stations are not at EPA headquarters or a regional office.
quote: Review telework policies and attorneys with permanent duty stations not at EPA headquarters or a regional office.

title: Pause and review large EPA grants
proposal: The chapter recommends pausing and reviewing all EPA grants above a set amount so grants go by need rather than ideology.
quote: Institute a pause and review for all grants over a certain threshold.

title: Put a political appointee in charge of EPA grants
proposal: The chapter recommends that a political appointee run the grants office and prioritize those most in need and projects with tangible environmental benefits.
quote: Put a political appointee in charge of the grants office to prioritize distribution of grants to those who are most in need

title: Cap research office grants
proposal: The chapter recommends limiting the number and size of grants the Office of Research and Development can give and requiring review by the Administrator's office.
quote: Cap the number and dollar amounts of grants that the Office of Research and Development can award

title: Fill EPA finance leadership with political appointees
proposal: The chapter recommends filling senior finance office jobs with political appointees, considering whether the deputy CFO should stay a career post, and creating a political Appropriations Liaison.
quote: should immediately fill these positions with political appointees and establish a new political leadership position for Appropriations Liaison

title: Review EPA travel and reimbursement policies
proposal: The chapter recommends reviewing EPA travel and reimbursement policies to match industry practices, and consolidating office space and security contracts.
quote: Review travel and reimbursement policies for best practices aligned for industry norms.
